# Public Star Driving School: full site content

Source: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/ . Generated 2026-11-05. Prices are in Canadian dollars; HST is 13%.

Public Star Driving School is an MTO-approved driving school in Ajax, Ontario, Canada, offering one-on-one G2 and G driving lessons, road test packages and the Beginner Driver Education (BDE) course with free pick-up and drop-off in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa. G2 lessons start at $50/hour + HST ($56.50) and G lessons at $60/hour + HST ($67.80).

## Key facts

- Business name: Public Star Driving School
- Type: Driving school (MTO-approved Beginner Driver Education provider)
- Address: 9 Graywardine Ln, Ajax, ON L1Z 0R9, Canada
- Phone (call or text): (437) 777-4494
- Email: publicstardrivingschool@gmail.com
- Website and online booking: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/#book
- Hours: 7 days a week, 8am to 9pm
- Service areas: Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby, Oshawa (east GTA and Durham Region, Ontario)
- Nearby DriveTest centres we train for: Metro East (Scarborough), Port Union (Scarborough), Downsview (North York), Oshawa
- Lessons: one-on-one, in dual-brake insured cars, free pick-up and drop-off at home, school or work
- Road test packages include use of the instructor's car and a warm-up lesson
- Help booking DriveTest road test appointments
- Lessons available in more than one language; ask when booking
- No payment needed to request a booking

## Prices

Full Beginner Driver Education (BDE) course, MTO-approved:
- Basic: $499 + HST ($563.87 total). Everything you need to earn your BDE certificate. Includes: 20 hrs online theory (self-paced); 10 hrs one-on-one in-car lessons; 10 hrs homelink assignments; Defensive driving & intersection techniques; Road test preparation; MTO certificate processing; Free pick-up & drop-off.
- Premium: $649 + HST ($733.37 total). Extra practice plus our car for your road test. Includes: Everything in Basic; 11 hrs one-on-one in-car lessons; Use of instructor's car for G2 road test; Road test booking assistance; Free pick-up & drop-off.
- Advanced: $799 + HST ($902.87 total). Maximum preparation for nervous or first-time drivers. Includes: Everything in Premium; 15 hrs one-on-one in-car lessons; Use of instructor's car for G2 road test; Road test booking assistance; Free pick-up & drop-off.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Do I need to complete the full BDE course to take lessons?
A: No. If you already have a G1 or G2, you can book individual lessons or an hours-plus-road-test bundle without enrolling in the full course.

Q: What does the BDE certificate get me?
A: Graduating from a Ministry-approved BDE course lets you take your G2 road test after 8 months instead of 12, and most insurers offer a discount for new drivers who complete it.

Q: Can I use your car for my road test?
A: Yes. Every hours-plus-road-test bundle and the Premium and Advanced BDE packages include the use of the instructor's car on test day, along with a warm-up lesson beforehand.

Q: How do pick-up and drop-off work?
A: Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace within our service area and drops you off at the end of the lesson, at no extra charge.

Q: How do I pay?
A: No payment is required to request a booking. We'll confirm your schedule first and arrange payment by e-transfer or in person before your first lesson.

Q: Can I book my DriveTest appointment through you?
A: Yes. We'll help you find and book an available road test slot at the DriveTest centre closest to you.

# How Many Driving Lessons Do I Need Before My G2 Test?

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/
Published: 2026-11-05. Updated: 2026-11-05.

Quick answer: Ontario does not set a minimum number of professional lessons for the G2 road test, but you must hold your G1 for 12 months first, or 8 months if you finish a government-approved driver education course. As a rule of thumb, drivers who already practise regularly with a family member usually need 2 to 5 hours with an instructor to fix habits and learn the test, while true beginners are better off with 10 hours or a full BDE course.

"How many lessons do I need?" is the first thing most new drivers ask us. The honest answer is that it depends on how much you have already driven, not on a number set by the government. This guide explains what Ontario actually requires, how to judge where you are, and how many hours make sense for different kinds of drivers in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa.

## Does Ontario require a minimum number of driving lessons?

No. Ontario does not require you to take any professional lessons before your G2 road test (the G1 exit test). What it does require is time:

- You must hold your G1 licence for 12 months before your first road test.
- If you finish a government-approved driver education course, you can take the road test after 8 months.
- You have five years to finish the whole graduated licensing process, or you start over.

So lessons are not a legal box to tick. They are there to get you ready to pass and to drive safely afterwards. If you are thinking about the 8 month option, our guide on whether the BDE course is worth it (/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/) walks through the trade-offs.

## How many lessons do most drivers need?

There is no official statistic on this, so we will not invent one. What we can share is a simple guide based on where you are starting from:

| Your situation | Suggested lessons with an instructor |
| --- | --- |
| You drive several times a week with a family member and feel confident | 2 to 3 hours, focused on test skills |
| You practise sometimes but still hesitate at left turns or lane changes | 4 to 5 hours |
| You have barely driven, or you are very nervous | 10 hours, or a full BDE course |
| You failed a previous G2 test | 2 to 3 hours on the items on your scoresheet |

These are starting points. Your instructor will tell you after the first lesson whether you need more or less.

## Signs you are ready for the G2 road test

Hours matter less than skills. Before you book, you should be able to do all of these smoothly, without someone in the passenger seat reminding you:

1. Full stops behind the line at every stop sign, then a clear look both ways.
2. Mirror, signal, shoulder check before every lane change and every pull-out from the curb.
3. Left turns at busy lights, waiting in the intersection for a safe gap.
4. Parallel parking and a three-point turn on a quiet street.
5. Residential driving at a steady speed, watching for pedestrians and parked cars.
6. Keeping a safe following distance in traffic.

Ontario lists these skills on its G2 road test page: left and right turns, stopping, parallel parking, one-way streets, lane changes, three-point turns, residential neighbourhoods, and traffic lights, stop and yield signs. If any of them still feels shaky, that is where your lessons should go.

For a full test-day checklist, read how to pass your G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/).

## Why practice with family is not always enough

Practising with a parent or friend is a great way to build hours behind the wheel. The catch is that family members often pass on habits that cost marks on a road test, such as rolling stops, skipped shoulder checks, or one hand on the wheel. They also may not know what examiners look for.

A few lessons with a certified instructor help you:

- Spot and fix bad habits before they become automatic.
- Learn the test format, including how the examiner gives directions.
- Practise on roads like those near your test centre, since DriveTest does not publish its routes.
- Avoid automatic fails, like the ones in our G2 road test automatic fails list (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/).

One more benefit: Ontario lets a G1 driver with a certified driving instructor drive on any road, so lessons are also a chance to try roads you cannot use with a family member.

## Should you book lessons all at once or spread them out?

Spread them out if you can. One or two lessons a week, with family practice in between, works better than five hours crammed into the week of your test. You get time to practise what the instructor taught you, then come back and fix what is still not right.

A good plan for most drivers looks like this:

- First lesson: a full assessment, so you know exactly what to work on.
- Middle lessons: focus on your weak spots, such as parking or busy intersections.
- Last lesson: a mock road test, then a warm-up drive on test day.

| --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson | $50 + HST ($56.50) |
| 2 hours + road test | $200 + HST ($226.00) |
| 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 4 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |

The road test packages include a warm-up before your test and the use of our instructor's car for the test itself, so you do not need to worry about a family car failing the vehicle check. The DriveTest road test fee is separate and paid to DriveTest. Check the current amount on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/).

If you want the 8 month option, our BDE packages are:

| BDE package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| Basic | $499 + HST ($563.87) |

## What if you are taking your test at a busy centre?

Many of our students test at Metro East in Scarborough or at the Oshawa centre. Both have busy roads nearby, so it helps to spend at least one lesson in that area. Our guides to Metro East DriveTest (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/) and Oshawa DriveTest (/blog/oshawa-drivetest-tips/) describe the kinds of roads you can expect.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is 2 hours of driving lessons enough for the G2 test?

It can be, if you already drive often and confidently with a family member. Two hours is usually enough to fix a few habits and run through the test. If you are still unsure about parking or busy intersections, book more.

### Can I take the G2 test without any lessons?

Yes. Ontario does not require professional lessons. You only need to hold your G1 for 12 months, or 8 months with an approved driver education course.

### How many lessons do I need if I have never driven before?

Start with an assessment lesson. Most complete beginners need around 10 hours with an instructor, plus regular practice, before they are ready. A BDE course is also a good fit and can shorten your G1 wait to 8 months.

### Do lessons have to be with a certified instructor?

To count toward the 8 month option, you need to finish a government-approved driver education course. Ontario lists approved driving schools on ontario.ca. Practice with a fully licensed family member does not shorten the wait.

### When should I take my last lesson?

Ideally within a few days of your test, followed by a warm-up drive on the day itself. That keeps the skills fresh without leaving you tired.

# Oshawa DriveTest: Road Test Tips for the Midtown Mall Centre

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/oshawa-drivetest-tips/
Published: 2026-11-04. Updated: 2026-11-04.

Quick answer: Oshawa DriveTest is in Midtown Mall at 200 John St W, Oshawa, and it runs road test appointments Monday to Saturday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The G2 road test costs $53.75 and the G road test costs $91.25, and DriveTest asks you to arrive at least 30 minutes early. The best preparation is practising on the busy downtown streets, residential roads and highway ramps around the centre so nothing on test day feels new.

Oshawa is the main DriveTest centre for drivers in Durham Region. Many of our students from Oshawa, Whitby, Ajax and Pickering book their G2 or G test there because it is close to home and they can practise on the same kinds of roads. This guide covers the practical side: where the centre is, when road tests run, what they cost, what happens after you check in, and how to get ready for driving in that part of Oshawa.

## Where is the Oshawa DriveTest centre?

DriveTest lists the centre as Oshawa at:

Midtown Mall, 200 John St W, Oshawa, L1J 2B4

The centre is inside a mall, so you park in the lot and walk in to check in. Leave extra time if you are driving in from Whitby, Ajax or Pickering. Highway 401 and the main east to west roads can back up at rush hour, and arriving late and rushed is a bad way to start a road test.

## Oshawa DriveTest hours and road tests offered

DriveTest's centre list shows Oshawa as a full-time centre that offers a wide range of road tests, including G2 and G for cars, M2 and M for motorcycles, and commercial classes.

| Service | Days | Hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inside services (licences, knowledge tests) | Monday to Friday | 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |
| Road test appointments | Monday to Saturday | 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |

Hours can change for holidays or bad weather, so check the DriveTest service disruptions page (https://drivetest.ca/find-a-drivetest-centre/service-disruptions/) on the morning of your test. DriveTest also notes that the G road test has been temporarily modified at full-time centres, so read the current G test description on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/road-tests-cars/) before you book.

## How much does a road test in Oshawa cost?

Road test fees are the same at every DriveTest centre in Ontario. These are DriveTest's current fees:

| Road test | DriveTest fee |
| --- | --- |
| Class G2 road test | $53.75 |
| Class G road test | $91.25 |

If you cancel or reschedule with less than 48 hours notice, or do not show up, you lose your road test fee. You can book and pay for G2 and G tests online. Always confirm the latest amounts on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/) before you book.

## What happens on test day in Oshawa

The process is the same at every DriveTest centre. Knowing it ahead of time takes a lot of the nerves away.

1. Arrive at least 30 minutes early. DriveTest asks for this at every centre.
2. Park and go inside to check in. Bring your licence and be ready to confirm your booking.
3. Go back to your car and wait. The examiner comes to you in the parking lot.
4. Vehicle check. Before you drive, the examiner checks that the car is safe. Lights, signals, horn, brakes, tires and the windshield all matter.
5. The drive. DriveTest says the G2 test usually takes about 20 minutes.
6. Results. The examiner gives you a short summary at the end along with your scoresheet.

A few rules catch people out:

- No passengers. Your instructor, friends and family cannot ride along. Only you and the examiner are in the car.
- No recording. Phones and dashboard cameras must be off during the test.
- No driving aids. Features such as automatic parking, lane keeping, cruise control and back cameras may not be used during the test. Practise parking with your mirrors and shoulder checks.
- Plan your ride home. If you take your G2 test on a G1, you cannot drive home alone if you do not pass, so bring a fully licensed driver or arrange another ride.

For the car problems and driving errors that end a test early, see our list of G2 road test automatic fails (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/).

## How to prepare for the roads around Oshawa DriveTest

DriveTest does not publish its test routes, and examiners can take you anywhere nearby. Instead of memorising one route, get comfortable with the kinds of roads you will meet around downtown Oshawa:

- Downtown streets. Expect traffic lights close together, buses, pedestrians and cars pulling in and out of parking spots. Some downtown streets are one-way, so read every sign and stay in the correct lane before you turn.
- Busy arterial roads. Multi-lane roads in Oshawa carry heavy traffic and lots of turning cars. Do a mirror check, signal and shoulder check for every lane change.
- Left turns at busy lights. Move into the intersection when it is safe, wait for a real gap, and turn into the correct lane. Never rush a left turn because someone behind you is impatient.
- Residential streets. Quiet side streets mean stop signs, school zones, parked cars and people walking. Stop fully behind the line, look both ways, and watch your speed.
- Leaving and entering the mall lot. Your test starts and ends in a parking lot. Drive slowly, watch for pedestrians, and signal when you pull onto the road.
- Parking and reversing. The G2 test checks parking and reversing, so practise until it feels routine.

If you are taking the G test, add highway practice on Highway 401 and Highway 407 ramps if you can. Our G road test highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) cover merging, lane changes at speed and exits, and our G2 vs G road test guide (/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/) explains how the two tests differ.

## Should you take your test in Oshawa or somewhere else?

There is no official ranking of "easy" DriveTest centres, and we will not make one up. Every centre uses the same scoring standards. The better question is which centre's roads you can practise on the most. If you live in Oshawa, Whitby or Courtice, Oshawa is usually the most convenient choice. Students in Scarborough often prefer Metro East DriveTest (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/), and some in Pickering and Ajax book Port Union. Pick the centre near where you can get real practice, then book early, because test dates can fill up.

For general advice that works at any centre, read how to pass your G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/).

With an hours plus road test package, you get lessons before the test, a warm-up drive on test day, and our instructor's car for the test itself, so you are not relying on a family car that might not pass the vehicle check. We offer free pick-up and drop-off in Oshawa, Whitby, Ajax, Pickering, Scarborough and North York.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the address of Oshawa DriveTest?

Midtown Mall, 200 John St W, Oshawa, L1J 2B4, according to DriveTest's centre list.

### Does Oshawa DriveTest do G road tests?

Yes. DriveTest lists Oshawa as offering G2 and G road tests, plus motorcycle and commercial classes.

### What time are road tests at Oshawa DriveTest?

DriveTest lists road test appointments Monday to Saturday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Check the service disruptions page on the day of your test.

### Can my driving instructor ride with me during the test?

No. Only you and the examiner can be in the car. Your instructor can drive you there, warm you up, and wait for you.

### Is Oshawa DriveTest harder than other centres?

There is no official data showing one centre is harder than another. What matters most is practising on roads like the ones around the centre you choose.

# Metro East DriveTest: Road Test Tips for the Scarborough Area Centre

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/
Published: 2026-11-03. Updated: 2026-11-03.

Quick answer: Metro East DriveTest is at Victoria Terrace Plaza, 1448 Lawrence Ave E, Unit 15, Toronto, and it runs G2 and G road tests Monday to Saturday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The G2 road test costs $53.75 and the G road test costs $91.25, and DriveTest asks you to arrive at least 30 minutes early. The best preparation is practising on the busy arterial roads and residential streets around the centre so nothing on test day is new to you.

Metro East is one of the busiest DriveTest centres for drivers from Scarborough, North York and East York. Lots of our students book their G2 or G test there because it is close to home. This guide covers the practical side: where it is, when road tests run, what it costs, what happens after you check in, and how to prepare for driving in that part of the city.

## Where is the Metro East DriveTest centre?

DriveTest lists the centre as Toronto Metro East at:

Victoria Terrace Plaza, 1448 Lawrence Ave E, Unit 15, Toronto, M4A 2V6

It sits in a plaza on Lawrence Avenue East, so you park in the plaza lot and walk in to check in. If you are coming from Scarborough, Pickering or Ajax, give yourself extra time: Lawrence and the roads that feed into it can be slow at rush hour, and you do not want to start your test already stressed about being late.

## Metro East hours and road tests offered

According to DriveTest's centre list, Metro East offers road tests for classes G2, G, M2 and M.

| Service | Days | Hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inside services (licences, knowledge tests) | Monday to Friday | 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. |
| Inside services | Saturday | 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |
| Road test appointments | Monday to Saturday | 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |

Hours can change for holidays or bad weather, so check the DriveTest service disruptions page (https://drivetest.ca/find-a-drivetest-centre/service-disruptions/) on the morning of your test.

## How much does a road test at Metro East cost?

Road test fees are the same at every DriveTest centre in Ontario. These are DriveTest's current fees:

| Road test | DriveTest fee |
| --- | --- |
| Class G2 road test | $53.75 |
| Class G road test | $91.25 |

If you cancel or reschedule with less than 48 hours notice, or do not show up, Ontario says your prepaid road test fee is not refunded. If your test is declared out-of-order because of the car, you lose 50% of the fee. Always confirm the latest amounts on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/) before you book.

## What happens on test day at Metro East

DriveTest's process is the same at every centre, but knowing it ahead of time takes a lot of the nerves away.

1. Arrive at least 30 minutes early. DriveTest asks for this at every centre.
2. Park and go inside to check in. Most centres have a self-serve kiosk; if not, see a customer service agent.
3. Go back to your car and wait. The examiner comes to you. If no examiner arrives within 30 minutes of your appointment time, DriveTest says to go back inside to Counter A.
4. Vehicle check. Before you drive, the examiner checks that the car is in good working order. Lights, signals, horn, brakes and the windshield all matter.
5. The drive. DriveTest says the G2 test usually takes about 20 minutes.
6. Results. The examiner gives you a short summary at the end and you get a scoresheet.

A few rules catch people out every week:

- No passengers. Your instructor, friends and family cannot ride along. Only you and the examiner are in the car.
- No recording. Phone, dashboard and action cameras must be turned off. If a camera cannot be turned off, you must confirm out loud that it is not recording the inside of the car or pointed at the examiner, or the test is declared out-of-order.
- No driving aids. Ontario's handbook says electronic aids such as automatic parallel parking, lane monitoring, cruise control and back cameras may not be used during the test. Practise parking with your mirrors and shoulder checks.
- Plan your ride home. If you are taking your G2 test on a G1, you cannot drive home alone if you fail, so bring a fully licensed driver or arrange another way home.

For the car problems that end a test before it starts, see our list of G2 road test automatic fails (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/).

## How to prepare for the roads around Metro East

DriveTest does not publish its test routes, and examiners can take you anywhere nearby. So instead of memorising one route, get comfortable with the kinds of roads you will meet in this area:

- Busy multi-lane arterials. Lawrence Avenue East and the main roads near the plaza carry heavy traffic, buses and lots of turning cars. Practise lane changes with a mirror check, signal and shoulder check every single time.
- Left turns at busy lights. Waiting in the intersection for a gap, then turning into the correct lane, is a skill examiners watch closely. Do not rush a left turn because someone behind you is impatient.
- Residential streets. Expect quiet side streets with stop signs, parked cars and pedestrians. Come to a full stop behind the line, look both ways, and keep your speed down.
- Leaving and entering the plaza. Your test starts and ends in a parking lot. Drive slowly, watch for pedestrians, and signal when you pull out onto the road.
- Parking and reversing. The G2 test checks parallel parking and reversing, so practise in quiet streets until it feels routine.

If you are taking the G test instead, add expressway practice. Our G road test highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) cover merging, lane changes at speed and exits, and our G2 vs G road test guide (/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/) explains how the two tests differ.

## Should you take your test at Metro East or somewhere else?

There is no official ranking of "easy" DriveTest centres, and we will not make one up. The better question is which centre's roads you can practise on most. If you live in Scarborough, North York or East York, Metro East is often the most convenient choice. Students in the east end sometimes prefer Port Union, and students in Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa often book Oshawa (/blog/oshawa-drivetest-tips/). Pick the centre near where you can get real practice, then book early, since test dates can fill up.

For general tips that apply to any centre, read how to pass your G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/).

# G2 Road Test Automatic Fails: What Ends Your Test in Ontario

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/
Published: 2026-11-02. Updated: 2026-11-02.

Quick answer: DriveTest does not publish an official list of G2 automatic fails, but examiners can stop the test if your driving puts safety at risk, so one dangerous action such as rolling a stop, failing to yield, an unsafe lane change or making the examiner step in usually ends it. Before you even drive, a car problem like a dead brake light, cracked windshield or active dashcam gets the test declared "out-of-order" and you lose 50% of your road test fee. After a fail you generally wait at least 10 days to retest.

Most students worry about parallel parking, but that is rarely what ends a G2 road test. Tests are usually lost in two ways: something about the car or the paperwork stops the test before it starts, or one dangerous action during the drive ends it early. This guide covers both, using DriveTest's own rules and what our instructors see on test day.

## Is there an official G2 automatic fail list?

No. DriveTest does not publish a list of "automatic fail" mistakes. What it does say is that the examiner scores you against set criteria on a scoresheet, and that the examiner may stop or refuse to start the test if:

- Your vehicle is not in good working order
- You show any signs of impairment from alcohol or drugs
- Your driving skills are not good enough to finish the test without risking safety

That last point is what people mean by an automatic fail. Minor errors are marked and added up. A single action that creates real danger can fail you by itself, however well the rest of the drive went.

## Driving mistakes that usually fail you on the spot

These are the actions our instructors see examiners treat as dangerous. One of them is normally enough to end the test:

- Rolling through a stop sign. Stop completely behind the line. If you cannot see, creep forward after the full stop.
- Not yielding the right of way to pedestrians in a crosswalk, cyclists, or a car that has the right of way at a four-way stop.
- An unsafe lane change. Changing lanes without a mirror and shoulder check, or forcing another driver to brake.
- Running a red light, or entering on an amber you could have stopped for safely.
- Speeding in a school zone or community safety zone, or driving well over the limit anywhere.
- The examiner having to intervene, by warning you or reaching for the wheel to prevent a collision.
- Hitting the curb hard or mounting it, or touching another vehicle or object.
- Turning left into oncoming traffic without a safe gap.
- Ignoring a school bus with its red lights flashing.

Notice the pattern: almost every item is about observation and judgment, not car control. Our G2 road test guide (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/) explains how to build the scanning habits that prevent these errors.

## Car problems that cancel your test before it starts

Before you drive, the examiner walks around your car and may ask you to test the signals and brake lights. If the vehicle does not meet MTO standards, the test is declared out-of-order. DriveTest lists many reasons. The ones that catch G2 students most often are:

| Problem | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| A brake light, turn signal, headlight or tail light that does not work | Other drivers cannot read your actions |
| Damaged windshield with large cracks or stars | Blocks the driver's view |
| Flat tire, temporary spare, or defective tires | Unsafe to drive |
| Horn or speedometer not working | Required safety equipment |
| Missing or broken seatbelt (yours or the examiner's) | Required for both people |
| Wipers or defroster not working, or no washer fluid, when the weather calls for it | Visibility |
| Missing mirror or rear bumper, or a loose plate | Vehicle is not roadworthy |
| A dashcam or phone camera that is recording | Recording devices must be disabled |
| Passengers or pets in the car | Only you and the examiner may ride |

An out-of-order test is not a fail on your record, but it still costs you. You lose 50% of your road test fee. The other half stays as a credit, and you pay the missing half to book again. This applies whether the car is yours, borrowed from family, rented, or a driving instructor's.

## Other things that end your test before you drive

Some problems have nothing to do with how you drive:

- Showing up with no vehicle. DriveTest does not provide cars.
- Not wearing glasses or contacts when your licence requires them.
- Refusing to wear a seatbelt.
- Booking through a BDE course when your driving school has not certified you by test day.
- Booking the wrong test class, such as a G2 test when you meant to book a G.

Most of these also cost 50% of the fee, so check everything the week before.

## What to bring so nothing goes wrong

DriveTest asks you to arrive at least 30 minutes early and bring:

1. A vehicle in good working order
2. Glasses or contact lenses, if you need them to drive
3. Enough gas for the test
4. Your current driver's licence
5. A printout of your road test confirmation email

Plan a ride home in case the test does not go your way. Remember that a G1 driver needs an accompanying driver, and that person cannot ride along during the test itself.

If you need to cancel, Ontario says to do it at least 48 hours ahead to avoid a cancellation fee. Check current road test fees on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/).

## What happens after a failed G2 test

At the end, the examiner gives you a short verbal summary, and your scoresheet shows where you lost marks. If you took the test on a tablet, you can download your results online within 15 days.

You can take as many road tests as you need while your licence is valid. DriveTest says you generally must wait at least 10 days between tests, and you pay the road test fee again. If your G1 expires before you pass, you have to start the process over.

Use the scoresheet. If you failed for a rolling stop, spend your next lessons on stops and intersections, not on parking you already do well.

## How to make sure none of this happens to you

The simplest way to avoid both kinds of problem is to prepare with an instructor and take the test in the instructor's car, so you are not relying on a family car nobody has checked against the list above. Every Public Star G2 hours plus road test package includes the car on test day and a warm-up drive first, with free pick-up and drop-off in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa.

| G2 package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson | $50 + HST ($56.50) |
| 2 hours + road test | $200 + HST ($226.00) |
| 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 4 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |

During those lessons, your instructor drives the roads around your DriveTest centre and points out the exact moments where students tend to roll a stop or miss a shoulder check. See our driving lesson price guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/) for the full list of options, or our G2 vs G road test guide (/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/) to see what comes after you pass.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a rolling stop an automatic fail on the G2 test?

It is one of the most common reasons a test ends. DriveTest does not publish an automatic fail list, but a stop that is not complete is treated as a safety risk. Always stop fully behind the line.

### Can you fail the G2 test before you start driving?

Yes, in effect. If your car has a broken brake light, a cracked windshield, a recording dashcam or another defect, the test is declared out-of-order and you lose 50% of your road test fee.

### How many minor mistakes can you make on the G2 test?

There is no published number. Minor errors are marked on the scoresheet and added up, so a few small slips will not fail you on their own, but one dangerous action can.

### How long do you wait to retake the G2 test after failing?

DriveTest says you generally must wait at least 10 days between road tests, and you pay the road test fee again.

### Can I use my parent's car for the G2 road test?

Yes. The car can be owned, borrowed or rented, but it must pass the examiner's vehicle check. Check every item in the out-of-order table the week before, or book a package that includes your instructor's car.

# G2 vs G Road Test: What Is the Difference in Ontario?

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/
Published: 2026-11-01. Updated: 2026-11-01.

Quick answer: The G2 road test (the G1 exit test) checks basic skills like turns, stops, parallel parking, three-point turns and residential driving, and you can take it after 12 months with your G1, or 8 months with an approved BDE course. The G road test (the G2 exit test) comes at least 12 months later and focuses on advanced driving: merging on and off expressways, lane changes at speed, intersections and business areas. The G test currently leaves out parallel parking, the roadside stop, the three-point turn and residential driving.

Ontario has two road tests on the way to a full licence, and people often mix them up. The G2 test is about proving you can control a car safely on everyday streets. The G test is about proving you can handle faster, busier traffic on your own. Knowing what each one checks helps you practise the right skills at the right time.

## The two road tests at a glance

Ontario's graduated licensing system has two levels. You pass the first road test to move from G1 to G2, and the second road test to move from G2 to a full G licence.

| | G2 road test | G road test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official name | G1 exit test | G2 exit test |
| When you can take it | After 12 months with a G1, or 8 months with an approved BDE course | After 12 months with a G2 |
| Main focus | Basic control and traffic rules | Advanced driving at speed |
| Highway driving | Not the focus | Merging on and off expressways |
| Parallel parking | Yes | Currently not included |
| Three-point turn | Yes | Currently not included |
| Roadside stop | Yes | Currently not included |
| Residential streets | Yes | Currently not included |
| Highway declaration form | No | Yes, required before the test |

## When you can take each test

G2 test: you can take your first road test after 12 months with a G1 licence. If you complete an approved Beginner Driver Education (BDE) course, that drops to 8 months. Our guide on whether the BDE course is worth it (/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/) explains the trade-offs.

G test: you can take it after 12 months with your G2 licence.

Ontario gives you up to five years to finish the whole process. If you do not get your full G in that time, you have to start over. That means the fastest path from a new G1 to a full G is at least 20 months.

If you fail either test, you must wait at least 10 days before you can take it again.

## What the G2 road test checks

According to ontario.ca, the G2 test covers the core skills every driver needs:

- Turning left and right
- Stopping
- Parallel parking
- One-way streets
- Lane changes
- Three-point turns
- Driving in residential neighbourhoods
- Traffic lights, stop signs and yield signs

The G2 test is slower paced, but it is very detailed. Examiners watch for full stops behind the line, proper shoulder checks, safe gaps before left turns and smooth control of the car. Small habits such as rolling a stop or forgetting to check your blind spot add up quickly. Our G2 road test guide (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/) walks through each manoeuvre and the common mistakes.

## What the G road test checks

The G test covers more advanced skills. Ontario lists:

- Driving on major roads and expressways, including merging on and off
- Turns, curves and lane changes
- Intersections
- Driving in business areas

Ontario currently says the standard G test does not include parallel parking, roadside stops, three-point turns or driving in residential neighbourhoods, because those were already covered on the G2 test. Rules can change, so check ontario.ca before your test.

With the slow manoeuvres removed, nearly all of your result comes from how you drive in moving traffic. Speed control, mirror checks, safe following distance and confident merging matter most. Our G road test highway checklist (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) breaks this down step by step.

## The highway declaration: only for the G test

Before the G test begins, you must complete a Declaration of Highway Driving Experience. It describes the driving you have done on highways with speed limits of at least 80 km/h.

If you do not have enough highway experience, the examiner will declare the test "out of order." You lose 50 per cent of your road test fee, and the other half stays as a credit on your record. To rebook, you pay the half that was deducted. Plan regular highway trips in the months before your G test so this never happens.

There is no highway declaration for the G2 test. G1 drivers are not allowed on 400-series highways or high-speed expressways with a posted limit over 80 km/h, unless they are with a certified driving instructor.

## How the restrictions change between levels

Each licence level comes with its own rules. Here is a short summary from the MTO driver's handbook:

G1 drivers must:

- Have zero blood alcohol
- Drive with a fully licensed driver with at least four years of experience in the front passenger seat
- Not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.
- Stay off 400-series highways and high-speed expressways (unless with a certified driving instructor)

G2 drivers must:

- Have zero blood alcohol
- Have a working seatbelt for every passenger
- If 19 or under, carry only one passenger aged 19 or under between midnight and 5 a.m. for the first six months, then up to three (exceptions apply if a fully licensed driver is in the front seat or passengers are immediate family)

All drivers aged 21 and under must have zero blood alcohol, whatever their licence class.

## Which test is harder?

It depends on the driver. Students who are calm and precise in quiet areas often find the G2 test comfortable but feel nervous on the 401. Students who drive to work on the highway every day sometimes find the G test easy but slip on G2 details like parallel parking.

A better question is which skills you are weakest at. If merging into fast traffic makes you tense, focus on highway practice before your G test. If parking and three-point turns are shaky, fix those before your G2.

## Fees and booking

You prepay the road test fee when you book. The current G2 and G road test fees are listed on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca). To avoid losing your fee, cancel or reschedule at least 48 hours before your appointment. MTO and DriveTest do not charge a fee just to book a road test, so be careful with any site that asks for one.

## How Public Star helps with both tests

Our instructors train students for the G2 and G tests around the Metro East, Port Union and Oshawa DriveTest centres, with free pick-up and drop-off across Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa. Every hours plus road test bundle includes the instructor's car on test day and a warm-up drive first.

| Package | G2 price | G price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson | $50 + HST ($56.50) | $60 + HST ($67.80) |
| 2 hours + road test | $200 + HST ($226.00) | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 4 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) | $360 + HST ($406.80) |
| 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) | $400 + HST ($452.00) |
| 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) | Not offered |

For a full breakdown of BDE, G2 and G options, see our driving lesson price guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the G test harder than the G2 test?

The G test is faster and includes highway driving, while the G2 test has more slow manoeuvres like parallel parking. Which one feels harder depends on your weaker skills.

### Do you parallel park on the G road test?

Not currently. Ontario says the standard G test does not include parallel parking, roadside stops, three-point turns or residential driving, because those are covered on the G2 test.

### How long after my G2 can I take the G test?

You need to hold your G2 licence for 12 months. You have five years in total to finish the whole licensing process.

### Can I skip the G2 test and go straight to G?

No. You must pass the G2 road test first, then hold your G2 licence for at least 12 months before you can take the G road test.

### Can I use a driving school car for both tests?

Yes. Public Star's G2 and G hours plus road test bundles both include the instructor's car on test day and a warm-up lesson beforehand.

# G Road Test Tips: Your Highway Driving Checklist for Ontario

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/
Published: 2026-10-31. Updated: 2026-10-31.

Quick answer: To pass the Ontario G road test, focus on the highway: build speed on the ramp, check your mirror and blind spot before merging, keep a safe gap and speed, and signal early for every lane change and exit. You can take the G test after 12 months with your G2, and you must sign a Declaration of Highway Driving Experience showing recent driving at 80 km/h or more, or the test is cancelled and you lose half the fee.

The G road test is the last step to your full Ontario licence. It is different from the G2 test: less about parking and quiet streets, much more about driving at speed on major roads and expressways. If you are comfortable on the highway, it is very passable. If you are not, it is the part that catches most people off guard. Here is what the test covers and a checklist our instructors use to get students ready.

## When you can take the G road test

You can book the G road test once you have held your G2 licence for 12 months. Ontario gives you up to five years to finish the whole graduated licensing process. If you do not get your full G in that time, you have to start over, so do not leave the G test until the last few months.

## What the G road test checks

According to ontario.ca, the G test covers more advanced driving skills and still includes the fundamentals:

- Driving on major roads and expressways, including merging on and off
- Keeping an appropriate speed and space around your car
- Signalling, turns, curves and lane changes
- Intersections
- Driving in business areas

Right now, the standard G test does not include parallel parking, the roadside stop, the three-point turn or driving in residential neighbourhoods. Those skills were already tested on your G2. Ontario has said this applies until further notice, so check ontario.ca before your test in case it changes.

That means almost all of your score comes from moving traffic. The highway section is where you need to be at your best.

## The Declaration of Highway Driving Experience

Before the test starts, you must complete and sign a Declaration of Highway Driving Experience. It asks how many times in the three months before your test you drove on a freeway or a highway with a speed limit of at least 80 km/h, and how long those trips were.

This matters: if you do not have enough highway experience, the examiner must declare the test "out of order" and cancel it, and you lose 50 per cent of your prepaid road test fee. Plan real highway trips in the months before your test, not just the week before.

## Highway driving checklist for the G test

Practise each of these until you do it without thinking.

### Entering the highway

1. Look ahead on the ramp. Find the gap you want to merge into while you are still on the ramp.
2. Build speed. Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic. Merging too slowly is one of the most common highway mistakes.
3. Signal early so drivers in the right lane know you are coming.
4. Mirror, then blind spot. Turn your head to check over your left shoulder before you move over.
5. Merge smoothly into the gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless traffic leaves you no choice.

### Driving on the highway

- Keep a safe following distance. Leave a gap of at least two seconds, more in rain or heavy traffic.
- Hold a steady speed at or near the limit. Watch for changes in posted limits and construction zones.
- Scan your mirrors every few seconds so you always know who is beside and behind you.
- Stay out of other drivers' blind spots and do not sit beside a truck longer than you need to.
- Keep right except to pass.

### Changing lanes at speed

1. Check your mirror.
2. Signal.
3. Shoulder check in the direction you are moving.
4. Move over gradually, keeping your speed.
5. Cancel your signal.

Examiners can only score what they can see, so move your head clearly for every shoulder check.

### Exiting the highway

- Know your exit early. Move into the right lane well before the exit.
- Signal before the exit lane begins.
- Slow down in the exit lane, not on the highway itself.
- Watch the ramp speed. Exit ramps often curve sharply, so brake before the curve, not in it.

## City driving still counts

Away from the highway, the G test still looks at turns, intersections and business areas. The habits that got you through your G2 still apply: full stops behind the line, left, right and left again at every intersection, and safe gaps before turning left. Our G2 road test guide (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/) covers these basics and the mistakes that cause an automatic fail.

## What to bring on test day

- Your G2 licence
- A car in good working order that is plated and insured
- Glasses or contact lenses if you need them to drive
- Payment for any test fee you have not paid yet

Arrive at least 30 minutes early. Only you and the examiner may be in the car, so friends, relatives and instructors cannot ride along. Driving aids such as cruise control, lane monitoring and back cameras may not be used during the test. For the current G road test fee and booking, check drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca).

## How lessons help before the G test

Many G2 drivers rarely drive on the 401 or the 407, so a few lessons focused on merging, lane changes at speed and exits make a big difference. Our instructors take students on the highways and expressways around the Metro East, Port Union and Oshawa DriveTest centres, with free pick-up across Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa.

| Public Star G package | Price | Total with HST |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 hour G lesson | $60 + HST | $67.80 |
| 2 hours + road test | $250 + HST | $282.50 |
| 3 hours + road test | $300 + HST | $339.00 |
| 4 hours + road test | $360 + HST | $406.80 |
| 5 hours + road test | $400 + HST | $452.00 |

Every hours plus road test bundle includes the use of the instructor's car on test day and a warm-up drive first. See our full driving lesson price guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/) to compare G2, G and BDE options.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is highway driving on the G road test in Ontario?

Yes. The G test includes driving on major roads and expressways, including merging on and off. You must also sign a Declaration of Highway Driving Experience before the test.

### Is parallel parking on the G road test?

Not at the moment. Ontario says the standard G test does not include parallel parking, the roadside stop, the three-point turn or residential driving until further notice, because those were covered on the G2 test.

### How long do I need my G2 before the G test?

You need to hold your G2 licence for 12 months. You have up to five years in total to finish the whole licensing process.

### What happens if I do not have enough highway experience?

The examiner must cancel the test as "out of order" and you lose 50 per cent of your prepaid road test fee. Drive on highways of 80 km/h or more in the three months before your test.

### Can I use a driving school car for my G road test?

Yes. Public Star's G hours plus road test bundles include the instructor's car on test day, plus a warm-up lesson beforehand.

## What a lesson price should include

When you compare driving schools, a lower hourly rate does not always mean a lower total. Check these before you book:

- Pick-up and drop-off. Ours is free anywhere in our service area. Some schools charge extra or ask you to come to them.
- The car on test day. Using a school car for the road test is often an add-on elsewhere. Our bundles include it.
- Lesson length. Make sure an "hour" is 60 minutes of driving, not including the drive to your home.
- HST. Some schools quote prices with tax and some without. We always show both.
- One-on-one time. Lessons should be just you and the instructor.

## How many lessons do you need?

It depends on how much you already drive. As a rough guide:

1. Brand new drivers usually do best with the BDE course or 10 hours plus road test.
2. G1 drivers who practise with family often need 3 to 5 hours to fix habits and learn the test route.
3. Experienced drivers from another country often need 2 to 3 hours to learn Ontario rules and what examiners look for.
4. G2 drivers going for their G usually need 2 to 4 hours, mostly on highway skills.

Book one lesson first if you are unsure. Your instructor can tell you after an hour how many more you are likely to need.

# How to Pass Your G2 Road Test on the First Try in Ontario

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/
Published: 2026-10-30. Updated: 2026-10-30.

Quick answer: To pass the G2 road test on your first try, practise full stops behind the line, check mirrors and blind spots before every lane change and turn, keep a steady speed at or just under the limit, and rehearse the roads near your DriveTest centre. Most fails come from poor observation, rolling stops and unsafe lane changes, not from parking.

The G2 road test is short, usually around 20 minutes, and it checks one thing: can you drive safely on your own in normal traffic? Examiners are not looking for perfection. They are looking for good observation, smooth control and safe decisions. Here is how our instructors prepare students to pass the first time.

## What the G2 road test checks

Your examiner scores you on everyday driving skills:

- Starting, stopping and moving off from the curb
- Left and right turns at controlled and uncontrolled intersections
- Lane changes with mirror and blind-spot checks
- Stop signs, traffic lights and right-of-way
- Speed control in residential and main roads
- One or more manoeuvres, such as a three-point turn, roadside stop or parking

Each mistake is marked on a score sheet. Small mistakes add up, and a single dangerous action ends the test.

## Mistakes that cause an automatic fail

These are the errors examiners treat as dangerous. One of them is usually enough to fail. For the full list, including the car problems that cancel a test before it starts, see our G2 automatic fails guide (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/).

- Rolling through a stop sign. Stop fully behind the line, then creep forward if you need to see.
- Not yielding the right of way to pedestrians, cyclists or cars that arrived first.
- Unsafe lane changes without a shoulder check, or cutting off another car.
- Speeding, even a little, or driving so slowly you hold up traffic.
- Running a red or amber light you could have stopped for safely.
- The examiner having to help, by speaking up or touching the wheel to prevent a collision.
- Mounting the curb or hitting anything.

## The most common reason students fail: observation

Most G2 fails we see are not about control. They come from not looking enough. Make these habits automatic:

1. Before every turn: check your mirror, signal, then check your blind spot.
2. At every intersection: look left, right and left again, even on a green light.
3. Every 5 to 8 seconds: glance at your mirrors.
4. Before moving off from a stop: check your blind spot on the curb side.

Move your head when you check. Examiners can only score what they can see, and eye-only checks are easy to miss.

## Tips for the day of your test

- Arrive early so you are not rushed. Bring your G1 licence and payment if you have not paid.
- Use a car you know. Taking the test in the same car you trained in removes one source of nerves. Our road test bundles include the instructor's car and a warm-up drive first.
- Expect a vehicle check. The examiner may ask you to show the signals, brake lights and horn work before you leave.
- Ask if you did not hear an instruction. Asking is fine. Guessing wrong is not.
- Do not give up after a mistake. One minor error rarely fails a test. Reset and keep driving safely.

## Practise the roads near your test centre

Each DriveTest centre has its own mix of roads, school zones and tricky intersections. We train students on the areas around:

- Metro East on Lawrence Avenue East (see our Metro East DriveTest tips (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/))
- Port Union in Scarborough
- Downsview in North York
- Oshawa

Knowing where the school zones, speed changes and busy left turns are makes the test feel familiar instead of surprising.

## How many lessons do you need before the G2 test?

If you have practised with family, 3 to 5 hours with an instructor is usually enough to fix habits and learn what examiners expect. Brand new drivers often need more; our guide on how many driving lessons you need before the G2 (/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/) helps you judge where you are. See our driving lesson prices (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/) for single lessons and road test bundles. Once you pass, our G road test highway checklist (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) covers the next step to your full licence, and our G2 vs G road test comparison (/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/) explains how the two tests differ.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many mistakes are allowed on the G2 road test?

There is no fixed number published. Minor mistakes are added up on the score sheet, and one dangerous action, like a rolling stop or an unsafe lane change, can fail you on its own.

### What is the most common reason people fail the G2?

Poor observation: not checking blind spots, mirrors and intersections clearly enough for the examiner to see.

### Is parallel parking on the G2 road test in Ontario?

You may be asked to do a parking manoeuvre, a roadside stop or a three-point turn. Practise all of them, because you will not know in advance which ones you get.

### Can I use a driving school car for the G2 test?

Yes. Every Public Star hours plus road test bundle includes the use of the instructor's car on test day, plus a warm-up lesson.

# Is the BDE Course Worth It in Ontario? Cost, Insurance and the 8-Month Rule

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/
Published: 2026-10-30. Updated: 2026-10-30.

Quick answer: For most new drivers, yes. An MTO-approved BDE course lets you take your G2 road test after 8 months with a G1 instead of 12, many insurers offer a discount to BDE graduates, and you get at least 10 hours of professional in-car training. At Public Star, BDE starts at $499 + HST ($563.87).

Beginner Driver Education, or BDE, is the Ministry of Transportation approved course for new drivers in Ontario. It is not required to get your licence, so the real question is whether the time it saves and the training you get are worth the price. Here is how to decide.

## What the BDE course includes

Every MTO-approved BDE course follows the same core structure:

- 20 hours of classroom or online theory, covering rules of the road, defensive driving and hazards
- 10 hours of one-on-one in-car lessons with a certified instructor
- 10 hours of homelink assignments, practical tasks you do with a family member or on your own

When you finish, the school submits your certificate to the Ministry.

## The three main benefits

### 1. Your G2 road test 4 months sooner

Without BDE, you must hold your G1 for 12 months before taking the G2 road test. With a BDE certificate, the wait drops to 8 months. If you need to drive for work or school, those 4 months matter.

### 2. A possible insurance discount

Many Ontario insurers give new drivers a discount for completing an approved course. The amount varies by company, so ask your insurer for a quote with and without a BDE certificate. For young drivers, the yearly saving can make up a large part of the course price.

### 3. Better habits from day one

Ten hours with a professional instructor builds correct habits before bad ones form. Students who learn only from family often pick up rolling stops or missed shoulder checks, which are exactly what examiners fail people for.

## What BDE costs at Public Star

| Package | Price before HST | Total with 13% HST | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $499 | $563.87 | Full BDE, 10 hours in-car, certificate processing |
| Premium | $649 | $733.37 | 11 hours in-car, our car for your G2 test, test booking help |
| Advanced | $799 | $902.87 | 15 hours in-car, our car for your G2 test, test booking help |

All packages include free pick-up and drop-off in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa. See all our lesson prices (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/) for single lessons and road test bundles.

## When BDE is worth it, and when it is not

BDE is usually worth it if you:

- Are a new driver with little or no experience
- Want to take your G2 test as early as possible
- Are under 25 and paying high insurance premiums
- Do not have a family member who can supervise lots of practice

You may not need BDE if you:

- Have already held your G1 for 12 months
- Already drive confidently and only need test preparation
- Are an experienced driver from another country

In those cases, a few hours plus a road test bundle is often the better value.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the BDE course mandatory in Ontario?

No. BDE is optional. It lets you take your G2 road test after 8 months instead of 12 and may lower your insurance.

### How long does the BDE course take?

The course is 40 hours in total: 20 hours of theory, 10 hours in the car and 10 hours of homelink. Most students finish in a few weeks, depending on how often they book in-car lessons.

### How much insurance do I save with a BDE certificate?

It depends on your insurer, age and location. Ask your insurance company for a quote with and without the certificate before you decide.

### Can I start BDE before my G1 is 8 months old?

Yes. You can take the course any time after getting your G1. The 8-month wait for your G2 road test is counted from the date you got your G1.
